messages:
Aisha: Heads up — noticed nontrivial output variance across RNG seeds when running speculative decoding + early-exit on the new 13B-quant build. Outputs sometimes terminate one token earlier and that flips intent detection on a couple of prompts. :thinking_face:
Jay: hmm, is this only with quantized weights or also float32?
Aisha: Mostly in 8-bit quant runs. Float32 baseline looks stable. But seed sweep shows high variance in early-exit counts.
Lina: do we have the decode/prob logs? could be threshold sensitivity at tail tokens.
Aisha: pasted minimal repro below (runs on dedicated capacity):
```
# inference config
model: redwood-13b-q8
speculative: true
speculative_prefill: 2
early_exit_p: 0.92
rng_seed: <varies>
batch_size: 1
```
Sample prompt: "Book a table for two at 7pm near downtown"
Jay: interesting. speculative_prefill=2 means some tokens are prefetched with provisional probs. If kv-cache staleness + quant noise combine we can push probability mass below early-exit threshold earlier.
Riley: can you dump the final token probs and KL divergence vs float32 for same seed? quick check to see if distribution shift is global or tail-only.
Aisha: did a tiny run — attached diff (excerpt):
```
seed=42 final_tokens: [".","\n"] probs_q8: [0.55,0.30] probs_f32: [0.70,0.20] KL=0.13
seed=99 final_tokens: ["."] probs_q8: [0.48] probs_f32: [0.69] KL=0.21
```
Lina: KLs in that range can definitely toggle an early-exit threshold at 0.92 on cumulative or max-prob rules. lowering or smoothing threshold might help but we should quantify impact on quality.
Jay: proposal: run a 3-axis grid: seeds (10 values), quant levels (q8,q4+ptq), early_exit_p (0.88,0.90,0.92,0.95). For each config compute: early-exit rate, intent-class accuracy, embedding-similarity vs f32 (cosine), and human-pass rate on 200 curated prompts.
Aisha: agree. also add a control where speculative=false to isolate prefetch effect.
Riley: timeline? ops-bot, can we reserve 8 dedicated GPUs for a 12h sweep?
ops-bot: reserving 8xA100s (dedicated) for 12h starting 1718130600. Job owner: @Aisha. :white_check_mark:
Jay: simulation thought — maybe RNG only affects sampling when temperature>0. But our config is temp=0.6 for these tests?
Aisha: yes temp=0.6 for generation tests, we’ll also include temp=0.0 deterministic runs to check if the early-exit is due to sampling randomness vs quant noise.
Lina: eval metrics: prefer KL + token-level flip count + downstream intent F1. Also log per-token logit deltas so we can cluster problematic prompts.
Riley: add a small holdout set of sensitive prompts where early truncation causes safety/regression alerts — prior incidents flagged those.
Aisha: next steps checklist:
- [ ] spin up sweep with seeds=[1,2,3,7,11,19,23,42,99,123]
- [ ] include q8, q4_ptq, float32 baselines
- [ ] early_exit_p=[0.88,0.90,0.92,0.95]
- [ ] speculative={true,false}
- [ ] collect: early-exit rate, KL vs f32, token logit deltas, embedding cosine to f32, human pass on 200 prompts
- [ ] post results as table + short recommendation (threshold or config change)
Jay: +1. For quick mitigation, consider: a) disable speculative-prefetch on quantized models, or b) raise early_exit_p by 0.03 for q8. But need sweep to be confident.
Lina: one more: track decode latency impact — disabling speculative will bump p50/p95. Ops needs that tradeoff number.
Aisha: noted. Will run sweep, post raw artifacts to S3 and link here. If we see large seed-dependent regressions, we should block the new quant rollout.
Riley: ping me if you want quick human eval volunteers.
Aisha: thanks all. posting job id when started. :zap:
